name: Olympus Mons
description: The tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons stands about 22 km high, nearly three times the height of Mount Everest.

name: Valles Marineris
description: A vast canyon system stretching over 4,000 km, Valles Marineris is one of the largest canyons in the solar system, dwarfing Earth's Grand Canyon.

name: Gale Crater
description: Home to NASA's Curiosity rover, Gale Crater is a 154 km-wide impact crater with a central mountain, Mount Sharp, offering evidence of past water activity.

name: Hellas Planitia
description: One of the largest impact basins on Mars, Hellas Planitia spans 2,300 km in diameter and reaches depths of over 7 km below the surface.

name: Elysium Planitia
description: A broad plain featuring volcanic activity, Elysium Planitia is where NASA's InSight lander studied Mars' seismic activity and subsurface heat flow.

name: Medusae Fossae
description: An enigmatic formation of soft, wind-eroded deposits that might be remnants of ancient volcanic ash or sedimentary layers.

name: Arabia Terra
description: A heavily cratered, ancient highland region that may have once supported lakes and rivers, providing clues about Mars' wetter past.

name: Cydonia
description: Famous for the 'Face on Mars' illusion, Cydonia contains a mix of mesas and valleys, once thought to be artificial structures.

name: Argyre Planitia
description: A massive impact basin thought to have once held an ancient Martian sea, surrounded by highland terrain and channels that suggest water activity.

name: Utopia Planitia
description: The landing site of NASA's Viking 2 mission, Utopia Planitia is a vast northern plain where underground water ice has been detected.
